evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: Outbox algorithm: domain mutation and serialized event are written in one local database transaction. A service-owned relay locks batches (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), publishes persistent messages with publisher confirms and only then sets published_at. Confirm/crash ambiguity creates duplicates, handled by consumers. Keep eventId stable across retries; partition/order by aggregate only where required and use revisions for stale updates. Acknowledge delivery after durable effects. TTL/retention, relay leases, retry budgets and replay tooling must be specified and tested with first handlers. M0 provides tables/design only, not working consumption or relays.

agrosphere-contracts/README.md:7: See AGENTS.md for scope and engineering rules. Estate Service now defines Milestone 1A business operations; Spatial Service defines Milestone 1B; other service APIs remain foundation placeholders. Architecture lives in the sibling agrosphere-architecture repository; versioned API/event definitions live in agrosphere-contracts. Do not add path dependencies to sibling projects.

agrosphere-contracts/README.md:17: Consumer transaction: insert (consumer_name,event_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; apply projection only when inserted, in the same transaction; commit before ACK. Publisher writes outbox with domain mutation; relay publishes persistent messages with confirms and marks published only after confirmation. Duplicates are expected. Bounded retries and DLQ handling are required before consumers ship. Estate Service implements its v2 relay in Milestone 1A; consumer handlers remain separate work. Validate forecast period ordering and business semantics in applications as JSON Schema cannot enforce them.

agrosphere-contracts/README.md:21: Estate OpenAPI now defines sixteen business operations and Problem Details, JWT scope, pagination and optimistic versions. evidence.excerpt: All 22 operations are under /api/v1/spatial and documented with typed schemas in the pinned and authenticated runtime OpenAPI.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: Collections/export are paginated with size <=100 and stable ordering. Queries require bounded bbox and limit <=100 and report truncation. Errors are RFC 9457 Problem Details with UUID correlation IDs. Geometry and layer revisions reject stale PUTs. Inline block history is capped at 1000 versions with an explicit 422 rather than silent truncation.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: JTS validates Polygon, MultiPolygon, Point and LineString without repair. It rejects malformed/unclosed rings, self-intersections, invalid holes, empty/degenerate inputs, unsupported CRS, altitude/nonfinite/out-of-range coordinates and oversized coordinate sets. PostGIS stores 4326 geometry, provides envelope/centroid and calculates hectares with ST_Area(geometry::geography)/10000. Raw degree-based area is never used as hectares. JTS planar area is used only to detect degenerate polygons.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: Point queries use ST_Covers (including boundaries); intersection uses ST_Intersects; within returns stored geometry covered by the supplied polygon. GiST envelope prefilters bound queries. Active block overlaps are compared in geography hectares with configurable tolerance. Available polygon parents cover children; parent changes cannot strand existing child features. Per-estate row locks serialize those checks, and conditional geometryVersion updates reject concurrent overwrites. Old snapshots remain accessible through block history; no operational/tapping/latex records are read or changed.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: GeoJSON import is a bounded JSON FeatureCollection wrapper, atomically validated/persisted in the calling request with a durable job/report. No partial features/events survive failed imports. Export preserves feature/reference identifiers, geometry versions, provenance, bbox, centroid and calculated hectares. 3D Tiles metadata is supported through layers; no renderer, client or terrain engine is implemented.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: Production Keycloak realm/client/claim provisioning and startup against the user's shared private Compose stack were not attempted; private identity/credentials and operator configuration are required. Tests use disposable infrastructure and a local OIDC fixture, not production Keycloak. Azure, Kubernetes, actual Cesium/Unreal/mobile clients and external asset availability are outside scope.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: Division lifecycle cannot be authoritative until Estate contracts expose it; existing geometry after lifecycle/membership changes needs reconciliation. Imports are synchronous, atomic and capped at 100 features/2 MiB by default; no CSV endpoint, background job worker, geometry repair, altitude/vertical datum, antimeridian workflow or general projected-polygon transformation is included. Explicit CRS conversion supports points in 4326/3857 only. History has a documented inline cap, exports require paging, and queries can be truncated by explicit limit. Retention, alerting, DLQ operator permissions, reconciliation scheduling, publisher lock-timeout sizing, image digest pinning and performance/load characterization remain deployment hardening tasks. Synthetic asset URLs intentionally do not resolve.

Any division-event or general CRS expansion needs an explicit follow-up contract/architecture decision. No automatic continuation is performed.

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: Domain changes and outbox insert share one local transaction. A scheduled relay locks committed due rows with SKIP LOCKED, sends persistent mandatory messages, waits for positive confirms/no returns, and marks publication only afterward. Bounded exponential retries retain failed rows and stable IDs. Broker acknowledgment followed by database failure can redeliver: consumers must atomically deduplicate eventId. Backlog/failure gauges, health/readiness, bounded pooling and graceful shutdown are configured.

evidence.head: e2a080f8c83339f20a3cb3e26506859da100c402
evidence.excerpt: "agrosphere-estate-service/docs/MILESTONE_1A_REPORT.md:38: Domain writes and mandatory outbox inserts share one JPA-managed database transaction. The dispatcher locks due rows with SKIP LOCKED and sends persistent mandatory messages to durable agrosphere.domain using publisher confirms. Returns, nacks and exceptions retry with configurable exponential backoff; exhausted events remain FAILED for operator-controlled replay. Publication defaults disabled while preserving outbox records. Confirmation/crash ambiguity permits duplicates with the same eventId. Consumers must deduplicate consumer_name/eventId transactionally, ACK after commit and reject stale revisions. No exactly-once delivery is claimed. The implementation follows the [Spring AMQP confirm/return API](https://docs.spring.io/spring-amqp/reference/amqp/template.html)."

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: Implement AgroSphere Milestone 1B Spatial Service and estate identity projection only. Read affected AGENTS.md files, architecture ADR-0008, the completed Estate Service report, infrastructure configuration and contracts 0.2.0 first. Preserve independent Git roots and service-owned databases. Consume the Estate Service v2 snapshots with transactional consumer_name/eventId deduplication, revision-aware updates, retry/DLQ/replay and reconciliation. Implement spatial-owned PostGIS geometry and RFC 7946 WGS84 API contracts, using canonical estate/block UUIDs without cross-database access. Reject new operational use of inactive blocks and label synthetic fixtures SIMULATED. Add contract/security/PostGIS integration and duplicate/out-of-order event tests. Validate builds, migrations, permissions and Docker, document actual results and blockers, and stop after Milestone 1B. Do not add operations, telemetry, AI, web/immersive functionality or deploy to Azure.

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: All twelve requested Git roots were inspected on main. Only Web had pre-existing uncommitted changes; no Web files were changed. Spatial, Telemetry, Analytics, AI and Immersive remain unchanged. No parent build, shared persistence model or sibling runtime source dependency was introduced.

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: TappingSchedule supports DRAFT/ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/CLOSED and versioned edits/lifecycle. TappingAssignment supports PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/MISSED/CANCELLED, scheduled/ad hoc creation, worker reassignment and explicit transitions. TappingRecord stores planned/actual trees, worker/estate/block/date, execution instants, notes and recording actor; missed reasons store validated code, remarks and authenticated actor. Audit instants are UTC; canonical estate timezone controls business dates. No latex weight or DRC exists.

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: V1__messaging_foundation.sql is preserved. V2__rubber_tapping.sql creates four operational tables, internal assignment/schedule/record/reason foreign keys, UUID keys, numeric/status constraints, version/audit fields and filter indexes. Schedule/date uniqueness permanently prevents regeneration; a partial worker/block/date index prevents duplicate noncancelled work. V2 adds outbox retry state/index and preserves existing published history (upgrade test executed). Estate/block UUIDs have no cross-service foreign keys.

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: Requests use Bean Validation and observed versions. Invalid transitions and contradictory retries return 400; authentication 401, authorization 403, missing objects 404, uniqueness/version conflicts 409, invalid Estate references 422, unavailable/malformed dependencies 503. evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: Domain changes and outbox insert share one local transaction. A scheduled relay locks committed due rows with SKIP LOCKED, sends persistent mandatory messages, waits for positive confirms/no returns, and marks publication only afterward. Bounded exponential retries retain failed rows and stable IDs. Broker acknowledgment followed by database failure can redeliver: consumers must atomically deduplicate eventId. Backlog/failure gauges, health/readiness, bounded pooling and graceful shutdown are configured.

evidence.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
evidence.excerpt: Issuer/audience/cryptographic JWT validation follows the existing platform. Roles and trusted estate_ids are enforced inside Operations for individual objects and collection queries. PLATFORM_ADMIN/PLANTATION_ADMIN are global; ESTATE_ADMIN/ESTATE_MANAGER manage scoped schedules and assignments; FIELD_SUPERVISOR manages scoped assignments; FIELD_WORKER executes only own scoped assignments using signed sub; AUDITOR/VIEWER read only. Additional read roles do not remove a worker's own execution permission or grant writes to others.
